Well, unless you are willing to work for free, you need a way to make money out of your hard work; when it comes to apps, there are essentially three ways to do that:

  • charge money to buy the app; it’s all good, but you now have a number of customers who paid a one off fee, yet expect their app to be supported indefinitely; now, if support only consists in bug fixing, it might be a fair expectation, and you will — or should — eventually reach a point when your app is reasonably bug free (well, no bug affecting usability that is); where this model doesn’t work is if your app requires some kind of backend service; this is going to be a recurring cost to you and is not going to be sustainable;
  • you release the app for free, but as an ads supported app; well, that’s a massive bummer for most end users, as ads can be intrusive and become seriously annoying after a while; I have ditched apps for that reason. Moreover, ads revenue might not be as lucrative to a dev as he might expect, and that might not cover your support / recurrent costs;
  • your give away the app for free but charge a recurring subscription for the service it provides; if the app does provide value to its end users this is probably the best approach IMHO for them as well as for the dev; covers your recurring costs, scales up with the number of users in a predictable way, and doesn’t nag the user with stupid ads...
